title: poa secunda subsp. juncifolia
intro: Poa secunda subsp. juncifolia, commonly known as Needle Grass, is a type of grass native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It is valued for its medicinal properties, which include potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects, as well as its use in wound healing and skin regeneration. The therapeutic actions of Needle Grass are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, promote tissue repair, and exhibit antioxidant activity. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects are thought to be a combination of flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other secondary metabolites present in the plant.
